# Ilaria RVC documentation

> A note from Ilaria

- [Ilaria RVC documentation](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/index.md): Ilaria RVC documentation
- [Getting started](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/start/getting-started.md): You can also run Ilaria RVC on Kaggle using its remote GPU. This option works even if your computer has no NVIDIA GPU. Ilaria RVC on Kaggle
- [RVC fundamentals](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/start/rvc-fundamentals.md): Retrieval-based voice conversion (RVC) takes a vocal recording and synthesizes a version with the character of a trained voice.
- [RVC models and files](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/start/models.md): An RVC model changes the timbre of an existing performance. The source recording still provides the words, phrasing and timing.
- [RVC Pitch Extractors (F0 Methods)](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/start/pitch-extractors.md): A pitch extractor (also called an F0 extraction method) is the algorithm or neural network that tracks the fundamental frequency (pitch, melody, and intonation) of the input voice over time.
- [RVC Embedders](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/start/embedders.md): An embedder (also called a content encoder) is the neural network that reads your input audio and converts what is being said or sung into numerical content features before the RVC voice model reconstructs it in the target speaker's timbre.
- [RVC Pretrained Base Models](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/start/pretrained.md): A pretrained base model (also called a pretrain) is a pair of starting checkpoint files: a Generator (G_.pth) and a Discriminator (D_.pth), already trained on hundreds of hours of multi-speaker audio.
- [Precision Training & Inference (FP16, FP32, BF16)](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/start/precision.md): Beginner-friendly guide to RVC precision modes (FP16, FP32, and BF16): what they mean, GPU compatibility, training vs inference, and how to avoid NaN or HalfTensor errors.
- [RVC PTH Files (.pth)](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/start/pth-files.md): Complete guide to RVC .pth voice model files: exported voice models vs raw G and D checkpoints, FP16 vs FP32 sizes, compatibility rules, and common errors.
- [RVC Index Files & Feature Retrieval (.index)](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/start/indexes.md): Complete guide to RVC .index files (Feature Retrieval): added vs trained index files, how to tune Index Rate, and how to rebuild a missing index.
- [RVC ONNX Files (.onnx)](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/start/onnx-files.md): Complete guide to RVC .onnx model files: why they are usually used for real-time voice changing on AMD and Intel GPUs via DirectML, and how they compare to .pth.
- [Choose an RVC app](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/reference/tools.md): Compare compatible apps for live voice conversion, file conversion, and training.
- [Troubleshooting RVC](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/reference/troubleshooting.md): Step-by-step RVC troubleshooting for beginners and advanced users: Windows/launcher errors, GPU/CUDA/DirectML, models, training, live mic, and cloud notebooks.
- [Glossary](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/reference/glossary.md): See RVC fundamentals, Models and files and Training for these terms in context.
- [Voice AI Safety, Privacy & Model Licensing](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/reference/safety-privacy-licensing.md): Practical guide to downloaded model safety (.pth vs .safetensors), voice consent, licensing, cloud notebook security, and protecting credentials.
- [GPU Performance & Troubleshooting](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/reference/gpu-performance.md): Cross-cutting guide to GPU utilization, VRAM, thermal/power throttling, CUDA vs CPU bottlenecks, and gaming conflicts in RVC apps.
- [Benchmarking & Performance Comparison](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/reference/benchmarking.md): How to measure RVC training speed, inference real-time factor, GPU Delay, end-to-end latency, VRAM, and thermal throttling with repeatable A/B tests.
- [Convert a recording with Ilaria RVC](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/conversion/voice-conversion.md): Voice conversion starts with a performance. The output usually follows the source words, timing, articulation, and pitch contour while changing the sound of the voice.
- [Improve RVC Inference Audio Quality](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/conversion/audio-quality.md): Code-verified guide to improving RVC inference audio quality in Ilaria RVC: diagnostic baseline, pitch, F0 methods, Index Ratio, Protect, Formant Shifting, Volume Envelope, and Post-Process.
- [Text to speech and RVC](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/conversion/text-to-speech.md): Text to speech (TTS) generates a source recording from words you type. RVC then applies a separate voice model to that recording.
- [Real-time voice conversion](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/conversion/real-time.md): For a recording or a cover, file conversion lets you render and compare several takes.
- [Stems and mixing](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/conversion/stems-and-mixing.md): A stem is an isolated part of a mix, such as the vocal or instrumental. RVC is easiest to control with a clean vocal on its own.
- [Prepare a voice dataset](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/model-training/dataset-preparation.md): Every clip teaches the model something about its target voice.
- [Train an RVC voice model](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/model-training/training.md): Training learns a target voice from a prepared collection of audio. Use this guide when you want to build a model from your own or authorized recordings.

## Ilaria RVC

- [Ilaria RVC overview](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/ilaria-rvc/overview.md): You can also run Ilaria RVC on Kaggle using its remote GPU. This option works even if your computer has no NVIDIA GPU. Ilaria RVC on Kaggle

### Installation

- [Installation and updates](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/ilaria-rvc/install/installation.md): Download the supported NVIDIA build from Hugging Face. Extract the whole archive into a writable local folder and run RUN_ILARIA_RVC.bat there.
- [Logs and recovery](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/ilaria-rvc/install/troubleshooting.md): Start with Pitch 0, a short dry WAV and one known-good model. Change one setting per test. See Inference controls for the effects and export options.
- [Files, source setup and maintenance](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/ilaria-rvc/install/source-layout.md): An inference export can be used for conversion.
- [System Requirements for Ilaria RVC](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/ilaria-rvc/install/requirements.md): Ilaria RVC runs locally on your PC using PyTorch 2.10.0 and NVIDIA CUDA.
- [Compatible GPUs](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/ilaria-rvc/install/gpu-compatibility.md): The Windows ZIP is about 5.00 GB. Extract it to a new folder and run RUN_ILARIA_RVC.bat, or RUN_ILARIA_RVC_LOGS.bat for logs. ContentVec and RMVPE are included.
- [Version history and release differences](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/ilaria-rvc/install/version-history.md): The latest Windows release is 2.5.1. Check your installed version under Other → Update Ilaria RVC. Use All changes so far there to browse the release notes.

### Cloud

- [Ilaria RVC in the cloud](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/ilaria-rvc/cloud/cloud.md): Compare Kaggle, Google Colab, and Lightning AI Studio to run Ilaria RVC in a browser when your PC lacks a supported local NVIDIA GPU.
- [Kaggle](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/ilaria-rvc/cloud/kaggle.md): Click Run All in the editor. You can also run the four code cells one at a time, from top to bottom. Wait for each cell to finish before running the next.
- [Google Colab](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/ilaria-rvc/cloud/colab.md): Run Ilaria RVC in a browser with a GPU supplied by the cloud platform. Choose a notebook below. Enable an NVIDIA accelerator before running the first cell.
- [Lightning AI Studio](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/ilaria-rvc/cloud/lightning-ai.md): Run Ilaria RVC in a browser with a GPU supplied by the cloud platform. Choose a notebook below. Enable an NVIDIA accelerator before running the first cell.

### Inference

- [Single and batch inference](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/ilaria-rvc/convert/inference.md): Open Single Inference, choose a voice and load a short, dry clip. Set Pitch and Index Ratio to zero.
- [Text to speech](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/ilaria-rvc/convert/speech.md): Use Inference → TTS to turn written text into a recording. You can listen to the generated speech directly or convert it with an RVC model.
- [Processing and export](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/ilaria-rvc/convert/advanced-inference.md): Open Inference Settings, select rmvpe, expand RMVPE High Register and turn on Enable high register.
- [Every Inference control explained](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/ilaria-rvc/convert/inference-buttons.md): Inference uses a trained voice to convert a recording. For a first test, upload a short clean WAV, select a voice, leave Pitch at zero and keep optional features off.

### Training

- [Datasets, Dataset Checker & Audio Analyzer](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/ilaria-rvc/train/datasets.md): Your dataset is the single biggest factor deciding how natural, clean, and expressive your RVC voice model will sound.
- [Training and checkpoints](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/ilaria-rvc/train/training-workflow.md): Select a dataset and choose compatible RVC architecture, sample rate, pitch guidance, embedder and generator/discriminator pretrains.
- [Embedders and pretrains](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/ilaria-rvc/train/embedders.md): Open Embedder Settings below Audio Processing. Auto reads stored model metadata and uses ContentVec when no embedder is recorded.
- [Training controls and workflow](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/ilaria-rvc/train/training-controls.md): Ilaria RVC 2.5.0. RefineGAN training and inference support 32, 40 and 44.1 kHz with RVC v2 and Pitch Guidance.
- [Queue, dashboard and alerts](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/ilaria-rvc/train/queue-and-dashboard.md): Configure the experiment in Training, confirm its dataset and model name, and add it to the Training Queue. Use distinct names for distinct configurations.
- [Every Training control explained](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/ilaria-rvc/train/training-buttons.md): Training creates a new voice model from recordings. For a first experiment, use a unique name, a small clean dataset and a compatible pretrained pair.

### Other

- [Model library and merging](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/ilaria-rvc/manage/model-library.md): Import, inspect, and manage RVC .pth, .index, .safetensors, embedders, and Voice Blender merges in Ilaria RVC.
- [Voice Blender (Merge Models)](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/ilaria-rvc/manage/voice-blender.md): In Ilaria RVC, the Voice Blender feature is located in the Other tab under Merge models.
- [Safetensors ↔ PTH Converter](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/ilaria-rvc/manage/safetensors-converter.md): Complete beginner-friendly guide to Ilaria RVC's Safetensors and PTH model converter in the Other tab, including metadata preservation and Move .pth to models.
- [ONNX ↔ PTH Converter](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/ilaria-rvc/manage/onnx-converter.md): In Other → Convert model weights, select an installed model or provide a file. Export a pitch-guided RVC HiFi-GAN model to ONNX for use in a compatible external client.
- [Audio Analyzer](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/ilaria-rvc/manage/audio-analyzer.md): Open Other → Audio Analyzer in Ilaria RVC to compare up to eight audio files using waveforms, spectrograms, average spectrum, pitch estimation, and level tables.
- [Every Other panel explained](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/ilaria-rvc/manage/other-buttons.md): Use Other to manage files, inspect or combine models, review audio and maintain the app.

## Other RVCs

- [Step-by-step guides by app](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/other-rvcs/app-guides.md): Use Ilaria RVC to train a model or convert a recording.

### Model Training and Inference


#### Applio

- [Install Applio and check the engine](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/other-rvcs/training/applio/installation.md): Applio has two download options that run the exact same engine - only the UI and installation method differ:
- [Install a voice in Applio](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/other-rvcs/training/applio/models.md): Put model downloads in a known folder and extract any ZIP there. Keep the publisher’s notes alongside the files. Use models from sources you trust.
- [Convert a recording in Applio](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/other-rvcs/training/applio/inference.md): Start with one short recording you can recognize instantly. Spoken test material could be “Could you put the blue book by the window?” followed by a quiet pause.
- [Train, evaluate and export a voice in Applio](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/other-rvcs/training/applio/training.md): A first run proves that your recordings, configuration and hardware can produce an export you can convert with. Work on copied recordings you have permission to use.
- [Use Applio with a microphone](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/other-rvcs/training/applio/realtime.md): Prove that your model works with one recorded clip before setting up live audio. Use headphones for monitoring so the microphone cannot re-capture the speakers.
- [Turn a short script into converted speech](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/other-rvcs/training/applio/tts.md): Applio uses an online Edge TTS voice to read your text and an RVC model to change the generated voice.
- [Applio Realtime on Cloud](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/other-rvcs/training/applio/cloud.md): Run Applio and its Realtime tab in the cloud using Google Colab, Kaggle, or Lightning.AI when your PC lacks a supported GPU.

#### RVC WebUI (Mainline - Original RVC)

- [Install RVC WebUI (Mainline - Original RVC)](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/other-rvcs/training/mainline/installation.md): RVC WebUI (Mainline - Original RVC) is the upstream Retrieval-based Voice Conversion WebUI. Use its browser interface for file conversion and training.
- [Convert recordings in RVC WebUI (Mainline - Original RVC)](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/other-rvcs/training/mainline/inference.md): Start with a short recording that you can hear clearly in a normal media player, plus an exported RVC model you have permission to use.
- [Train and export a RVC WebUI (Mainline - Original RVC) model](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/other-rvcs/training/mainline/training.md): Start with a single speaker and a fresh experiment name. Training produces a model you can test on new performances in the inference interface.
- [Use the RVC WebUI (Mainline - Original RVC) real-time voice changer](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/other-rvcs/training/mainline/realtime.md): This guide applies to the separate real-time GUI included in supported RVC WebUI (Mainline - Original RVC) builds.

#### Redpanda-vc

- [Set up Redpanda VC](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/other-rvcs/training/redpanda/first-run.md): Start with the Windows x64 precompiled release. The desktop app uses Tauri and runs its Python voice engines locally. The source checkout also includes a browser WebUI with the same interface.
- [File inference](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/other-rvcs/training/redpanda/inference.md): Use Inference to convert a recording or an entire folder. An RVC voice uses a compact .pth model; a Causal Voice Changer voice uses .cvc.
- [Realtime voice conversion](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/other-rvcs/training/redpanda/live-audio.md): Open Realtime in the desktop app or browser WebUI. Test a single voice directly through headphones before sending the sound to Discord, OBS, a game or another app.
- [Train RVC Models in Redpanda-vc - EMA & Step-Based Saving](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/other-rvcs/training/redpanda/training.md): Beginner-friendly, code-verified guide to training RVC models in Redpanda-vc: Generator EMA, step-based checkpoint saving, resuming, exporting, and troubleshooting.
- [Causal Voice Changer training](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/other-rvcs/training/redpanda/causal-training.md): Redpanda’s Causal Voice Changer option integrates Causal Voice Changer v0.4.0. Fine-tuning creates a .cvc voice for the CVC engine.
- [Redpanda VC compared with other RVC apps](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/other-rvcs/training/redpanda/differences.md): Redpanda VC combines RVC and Causal Voice Changer in a shared desktop and browser interface. Older Redpanda builds used Gradio and included engines and tools removed from the current release.

#### rvc-cli

- [rvc-cli · Installation](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/other-rvcs/training/rvc-cli/installation.md): GitHub · Reviewed version
- [rvc-cli · Usage and troubleshooting](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/other-rvcs/training/rvc-cli/usage.md): GitHub · Reviewed version

#### RVC Studio

- [RVC Studio · Installation](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/other-rvcs/training/rvc-studio/installation.md): GitHub · Hugging Face · 91c4011
- [RVC Studio · Usage and troubleshooting](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/other-rvcs/training/rvc-studio/usage.md): GitHub · Hugging Face · 91c4011

#### Mangio RVC Fork

- [Mangio RVC Fork · Installation](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/other-rvcs/training/mangio/installation.md): GitHub · Reviewed version
- [Mangio RVC Fork · Usage and troubleshooting](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/other-rvcs/training/mangio/usage.md): GitHub · Reviewed version

#### AICoverMaker

- [AICoverMaker · Installation](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/other-rvcs/training/aicovermaker/installation.md): AICoverMaker is Eddycrack864’s Applio fork for producing voice-converted covers. This guide follows the v1.0.5 release. Start with a recording and a voice model you have permission to use.
- [AICoverMaker · First cover](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/other-rvcs/training/aicovermaker/usage.md): A cover on this workflow starts from recorded audio. The separator extracts a vocal stem, RVC changes the voice, and the result is mixed with the backing track.

#### Replay

- [Replay · Installation and availability](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/other-rvcs/training/replay/installation.md): Replay is discontinued following the closure of Weights.gg. The archive preserves version 8.7.0 installers. Setup may fail when it tries to download dependencies that were hosted by Weights.
- [Replay · Existing projects and training](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/other-rvcs/training/replay/usage.md): If you already have a working copy, keep it and back up your original audio, exported conversions and any model files you can access. Replay historically offered file conversion and model training.

#### AICoverGen

- [AICoverGen · Installation](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/other-rvcs/training/aicovergen/installation.md): GitHub
- [AICoverGen · Usage and troubleshooting](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/other-rvcs/training/aicovergen/usage.md): GitHub

### Voice Changers


#### Vonovox

- [Install Vonovox](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/other-rvcs/voice-changers/vonovox/installation.md): Vonovox is a Windows live voice converter for supported NVIDIA GPUs. Use this guide to reach a clean local microphone test before opening Discord, OBS, or a game.
- [Route and tune Vonovox](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/other-rvcs/voice-changers/vonovox/live-audio.md): Use three endpoints: your physical microphone for input, a virtual cable for the converted signal, and headphones for monitoring.
- [Advanced Performance Optimization: NVIDIA GPU Clock Locking](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/other-rvcs/voice-changers/vonovox/advanced-performance-optimization.md): Optional NVIDIA GPU Clock Locking guide to test whether locking supported graphics clocks improves Vonovox latency stability on Windows.

#### w-okada VCClient

- [Install w-okada VCClient](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/other-rvcs/voice-changers/okada/installation.md): VCClient converts live microphone audio. The interface is the client and the conversion process is the server. For your first test, run both on the same computer.
- [Convert your microphone in w-okada VCClient](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/other-rvcs/voice-changers/okada/live-audio.md): Start with headphones and a single local audio path. When you hear a clean converted voice in the headphones, connect it to a call or recorder.

#### Okada TG Developed Fork

- [Install Okada TG Developed Fork](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/other-rvcs/voice-changers/tgr/installation.md): TG Developed Fork (TGR) comes from the Deiteris branch of the w-okada family. The publisher documents this fork as RVC-only.
- [Set up live audio in Okada TG Developed Fork](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/other-rvcs/voice-changers/tgr/live-audio.md): Use a compatible RVC inference checkpoint and a working microphone. First prove that the converted signal reaches your headphones.
- [Okada TG Developed Fork on Cloud](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/other-rvcs/voice-changers/tgr/cloud.md): Run Okada TG Developed Fork in the cloud using Google Colab, Kaggle, or Lightning.AI when your PC lacks a supported local GPU.

#### Deiteris w-okada Fork

- [Install Deiteris w-okada Fork](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/other-rvcs/voice-changers/deiteris/installation.md): Deiteris w-okada Fork is a popular community-maintained fork of w-okada/voice-changer (VCClient) focused on lower latency, cleaner audio, stability fixes, and updated backends for modern NVIDIA (CUDA), AMD/Intel (DirectML), and Apple Silicon hardware.
- [Route and tune Deiteris w-okada Fork](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/other-rvcs/voice-changers/deiteris/live-audio.md): Always wear headphones during live conversion. Using speakers feeds the converted voice back into your microphone and creates echo and feedback loops.
- [Deiteris w-okada Fork on Cloud](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/other-rvcs/voice-changers/deiteris/cloud.md): Run Deiteris w-okada Fork in the cloud using Google Colab, Kaggle, or Lightning.AI when your PC lacks a supported local GPU.

#### RVC GUI

- [Install and convert with RVC GUI](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/other-rvcs/voice-changers/rvc-gui/file-conversion.md): This guide covers Tiger14n's archived desktop app for converting audio files. Prepare a voice checkpoint and a short, dry WAV recording before you start.

#### RVC Blue

- [RVC Blue (RVC-Realtime-GUI)](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/other-rvcs/voice-changers/rvc-blue/installation.md): RVC Blue is a Windows desktop voice changer based on RVC WebUI (Mainline - Original RVC)'s real-time GUI.

### RVC Model Merger

- [RVC Model Merger](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/other-rvcs/rvc-model-merger/usage.md): How to install and use RVC Model Merger by Ardha27 to blend two compatible RVC v2 voice models with adjustable merge ratios.

## Non-RVC & Audio Tools


### Voice Changers


#### YuneVoix

- [YuneVoix (YUNE)](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/non-rvc/voice-changers/yunevoix/overview.md): YuneVoix is a real-time AI voice conversion application for Windows, powered by the YUNE engine.
- [Install and update YuneVoix](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/non-rvc/voice-changers/yunevoix/installation.md): YuneVoix is a portable Windows application: nothing is installed into Windows, and all settings, voices, logs, and licences live next to YuneVoix.exe.
- [Voice Bank and Live Usage](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/non-rvc/voice-changers/yunevoix/usage.md): Complete beginner tutorial for creating Voice Bank .yvoice profiles, routing YuneVoix into Discord, OBS, games, or VRChat, using built-in monitoring, and choosing Classic, Learned 4 steps, or FlowEdit 3+1.
- [YuneVoix Settings Explained - Complete Audio Quality Guide](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/non-rvc/voice-changers/yunevoix/settings.md): Complete beginner-friendly guide to every YuneVoix v0.7.1 setting across General, Voice & Timbre, Pitch & Autotune, EQ & Filters, and Effects.
- [YuneVoix Song Cover & Karaoke - Complete Beginner Guide](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/non-rvc/voice-changers/yunevoix/song-cover-karaoke.md): Complete beginner tutorial for YuneVoix PREMIUM offline Song Cover and Karaoke features, including FlowEdit source differences, controls, keyboard shortcuts, and troubleshooting.
- [Premium, Licensing, and Troubleshooting](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/non-rvc/voice-changers/yunevoix/premium-and-troubleshooting.md): YuneVoix PREMIUM licensing (Song Cover & Karaoke), offline activation, hardware rules, expanded NVIDIA & AMD troubleshooting, and diagnostics.
- [YuneVoix Changelog](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/non-rvc/voice-changers/yunevoix/changelog.md): Complete YuneVoix release history and changelog from v0.6.0 through v0.7.1, including DirectML, AMD GPU, WavLM+, and FlowEdit 3+1 updates.

#### Causal Voice Changer

- [Causal Voice Changer (CVC)](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/non-rvc/voice-changers/causal-voice-changer/overview.md): Causal Voice Changer (CVC) is a 48 kHz real-time AI voice changer built to bridge the gap between ultra-low-latency systems (like Beatrice) and slower, high-fidelity systems (like RVC).
- [Installing Causal Voice Changer](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/non-rvc/voice-changers/causal-voice-changer/installation.md): This guide walks you through installing Causal Voice Changer on Windows or Linux, even if you have never used Python or Git before.
- [Training a Voice in CVC](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/non-rvc/voice-changers/causal-voice-changer/training.md): Building a voice in Causal Voice Changer fine-tunes the base decoder on your target audio.
- [Using CausalVC Realtime](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/non-rvc/voice-changers/causal-voice-changer/realtime.md): Once you have run run-training at least once and have a .cvc voice ready, launch the live voice changer with:
- [Performance, Sound Cleanup & Extra Tools](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/non-rvc/voice-changers/causal-voice-changer/performance-and-tools.md): You can record your sessions directly inside CausalVC Realtime (start conversion first):
- [Causal Voice Changer Changelog](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/non-rvc/voice-changers/causal-voice-changer/changelog.md): Complete Causal Voice Changer (CVC) release history and changelog from v0.1.0 through v0.3.3.1, covering older NVIDIA GPU support, 100 Hz v4 base, and realtime fixes.
- [Compatible GPUs for Causal Voice Changer](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/non-rvc/voice-changers/causal-voice-changer/gpu-compatibility.md): Complete list of compatible NVIDIA, AMD Radeon, and CPU setups for Causal Voice Changer (CVC), including v0.3.3.1 support for older GTX 900/10 GPUs.

### Audio Separation Tools


#### UVR5

- [Ultimate Vocal Remover (UVR5)](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/non-rvc/audio-separation-tools/uvr5/overview.md): UVR5 (Ultimate Vocal Remover v5 GUI) is a free, open-source desktop application for AI audio source separation.
- [Download and Install UVR5](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/non-rvc/audio-separation-tools/uvr5/installation.md): The official Windows and macOS packages include an isolated Python and PyTorch environment, so you do not need to install Python separately.
- [UVR5 Guide & Recommended Models](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/non-rvc/audio-separation-tools/uvr5/usage-and-models.md): Use this guide to configure UVR5 properly and pick the best models for separating vocals, removing harmonies/backing vocals, stripping reverb/echo, and cleaning noise (including the exact models shown in the recommended setups).
- [Ultimate Vocal Remover 6 (UVR6): Preparatory Guide](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/non-rvc/audio-separation-tools/uvr5/uvr6-preparation.md): Preparatory overview of Ultimate Vocal Remover 6 (UVR6), officially scheduled for Windows on December 11, 2026.

#### MVSep

- [MVSep](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/non-rvc/audio-separation-tools/mvsep/overview.md): MVSep (Music & Voice Separation) is a free, cloud-based AI audio separation and restoration web platform.
- [Using MVSep: Access, Account & Setup](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/non-rvc/audio-separation-tools/mvsep/access-and-setup.md): Because MVSep runs in the cloud, there is nothing to install. However, configuring your account and output settings properly makes a big difference in quality and convenience.
- [MVSep Guide: Recommended Models & Presets](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/non-rvc/audio-separation-tools/mvsep/usage-and-models.md): Below are the best MVSep presets for preparing ultra-clean vocal tracks (for RVC training, covers, or voice conversion), complete with direct links that pre-select the exact separation algorithm and options for you.

### TTS

- [Microsoft Edge TTS](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/non-rvc/tts/edge.md): Open a page in Microsoft Edge and choose Read aloud from the browser menu where available. Use Voice options to select a language, voice and reading speed. Immersive Reader can make supported pages easier to read and listen to.
- [Kokoro TTS](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/non-rvc/tts/kokoro.md): This guide uses the standalone CLI by nazdridoy. It generates speech from text with preset voices. Install it in an isolated Python environment or with uv tool install kokoro-tts.
- [GPT-SoVITS](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/non-rvc/tts/gpt-sovits.md): GPT-SoVITS generates speech from written text using a sample as a voice reference. Zero-shot inference uses a reference with an existing base model. Fine-tuning uses a prepared collection of clips and transcripts to adapt the model.

### Other Audio Stuff


#### Ilaria Audio Upscaler

- [Ilaria Audio Upscaler](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/non-rvc/other-audio-stuff/ilaria-audio-upscaler/overview.md): GitHub · v1
- [Installation and models](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/non-rvc/other-audio-stuff/ilaria-audio-upscaler/installation.md): GitHub · v1
- [Restore speech with Sidon](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/non-rvc/other-audio-stuff/ilaria-audio-upscaler/sidon.md): Choose Sidon, download Sidon INT8, add a short noisy or reverberant clip, select WAV (PCM) and run Enhance audio. Listen for quieter pauses and clearer words.
- [Extend speech bandwidth with AP-BWE](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/non-rvc/other-audio-stuff/ilaria-audio-upscaler/ap-bwe.md): Choose AP-BWE and match the first number in the profile to the usable bandwidth of the speech. An 8 kHz signal carries frequencies up to about 4 kHz. A call saved as a 48 kHz WAV can still have that narrow bandwidth.
- [Preview, export and troubleshooting](https://docs.ilariarvc.shop/non-rvc/other-audio-stuff/ilaria-audio-upscaler/export.md): Add one or more files, choose a format and run Enhance audio. Compare the original and enhanced audio in the player at 1×. Speed changes playback only. Select the enhanced result and click Save result to store it permanently.
